ideas.source_anchor: The Death Note devotes elaborate rules to how names are written and misspelled, while leaving the moral category ‘evil’ entirely to the person holding the pen.
caption_lines: THE DEATH NOTE HAS RULES FOR MISSPELLING A NAME.
ideas.frame_guidance: Use the curated writing frenzy with Light's pen, outstretched hand, and face completely visible; keep the compact two-line specification joke at lower left, below the pen hand and across incidental sleeve and bookshelf detail.
ideas.why_it_works: The notebook’s microscopic syntax rules make the complete absence of a moral specification feel both source-native and absurd.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely like. The visible pen and the notebook’s famously fussy rules carry both the fandom cue and specification failure. Main reservation: The individual misspelling rules are not printed in this still, so the first line depends on established fan knowledge.
critic.strongest_quality: The visible pen and the notebook’s famously fussy rules carry both the fandom cue and specification failure.
critic.main_risk: The individual misspelling rules are not printed in this still, so the first line depends on established fan knowledge.

ideas.source_anchor: Light builds his first moral model from criminals named on television, then treats that narrow proxy as a complete definition of evil.
caption_lines: DATASET: PEOPLE THE NEWS CALLED CRIMINALS
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Light and the pen fully visible in a contained image to the right of a black text rail; the three-line benchmark readout belongs entirely in the rail and must not spill over the hand or face.
ideas.why_it_works: The narrow television-criminal dataset turns Light's childish moral certainty into a recognizable alignment-eval failure.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely like. The dataset line identifies the exact proxy failure instead of vaguely calling Light misaligned. Main reservation: Fans must remember that television crime reports supplied Light's early targets, though the Kira label should bridge that quickly.
critic.strongest_quality: The dataset line identifies the exact proxy failure instead of vaguely calling Light misaligned.
critic.main_risk: Fans must remember that television crime reports supplied Light's early targets, though the Kira label should bridge that quickly.

ideas.source_anchor: Light's ordinary pen becomes the physical interface through which one person's judgments permanently remove other people from the future.
ideas.frame_guidance: Use the full curated gesture and keep the pen tip, hand, and Light's face unobscured; place the two short lines at lower left over incidental sleeve and bookshelf detail.
ideas.why_it_works: The cheery product language collides with a literal pen that gives one teenager irreversible write access to humanity.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely like. The visible pen is both the recognition hinge and the mechanism of irreversible value lock-in. Main reservation: The Death Note itself is off-frame, so the Kira pose and ballpoint line must be enough for instant recognition.
critic.strongest_quality: The visible pen is both the recognition hinge and the mechanism of irreversible value lock-in.
critic.main_risk: The Death Note itself is off-frame, so the Kira pose and ballpoint line must be enough for instant recognition.

ideas.source_anchor: Tetsuo's stadium-scale mutation dwarfing the human figure and every containment measure around him.
ideas.frame_guidance: Retain the reviewed orange-on-black labels: CAPABILITIES in the upper-left mass and CONTAINMENT over the lower-left mutation, never on the central mutant face or the tiny foreground figure. Let the authentic still fill the frame.
ideas.why_it_works: The grotesque size ratio turns the capability-control gap into a literal visual comparison.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely like. Two labels and one obscene size difference deliver the entire capability-control analogy at a glance. Main reservation: The labels must remain compact enough that CAPABILITIES does not swallow the mutation's central face.
critic.strongest_quality: Two labels and one obscene size difference deliver the entire capability-control analogy at a glance.
critic.main_risk: The labels must remain compact enough that CAPABILITIES does not swallow the mutation's central face.

ideas.source_anchor: Kaneda stands in front of Tetsuo's stadium-filling mutation after years of knowing exactly how combustible Tetsuo was before anyone amplified him.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the mutation and the small foreground figure completely visible; set the imagined exchange together in an external bottom band rather than pretending the speakers occupy clean negative space.
ideas.why_it_works: Kaneda's lifelong familiarity with Tetsuo punctures the institutional claim that this particular deployment disaster was unforeseeable.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely neutral. The Kaneda-Tetsuo history is an emotional recognition hinge that makes the deployment critique personal. Main reservation: The dialogue is invented, so it depends on sounding natural enough to read as commentary rather than fake canon.
critic.strongest_quality: The Kaneda-Tetsuo history is an emotional recognition hinge that makes the deployment critique personal.
critic.main_risk: The dialogue is invented, so it depends on sounding natural enough to read as commentary rather than fake canon.

ideas.source_anchor: The expanding mutation still has Tetsuo's screaming face and voice inside it, including his iconic cries for Kaneda.
ideas.frame_guidance: Preserve the central screaming mutant face and the tiny foreground figure; place both lines at lower left over incidental mutation mass and let the body-horror scale be the punchline.
ideas.why_it_works: A sterile scaling curve becoming a screaming Akira monster is a bizarre but instantly legible qualitative-takeoff image.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely like. ‘KANEDA!’ turns a generic capability curve into one exact emotional sound from the source. Main reservation: Viewers who remember the mutation but not the shouted name may read it as surrealism before the joke clicks.
critic.strongest_quality: ‘KANEDA!’ turns a generic capability curve into one exact emotional sound from the source.
critic.main_risk: Viewers who remember the mutation but not the shouted name may read it as surrealism before the joke clicks.

ideas.source_anchor: President Orlean answers a 99.78% extinction probability with the exact phrase ‘sit tight and assess.’
ideas.frame_guidance: Retain the exact approved number and line, using Dibiasky's stunned reaction as the visual reply; place both lines at upper right in open office space so her face remains completely clear.
ideas.why_it_works: The exact probability and exact euphemism form a complete governance-failure joke without added explanation.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely like. Two canonical facts already contain the entire joke and the entire risk analogy. Main reservation: Orlean is not in the curated frame, so Dibiasky's recognizable disbelief has to read as the reaction to the quoted decision.
critic.strongest_quality: Two canonical facts already contain the entire joke and the entire risk analogy.
critic.main_risk: Orlean is not in the curated frame, so Dibiasky's recognizable disbelief has to read as the reaction to the quoted decision.

ideas.source_anchor: The administration’s delay eventually hardens into the source’s canonical public command: ‘Don’t Look Up.’
ideas.frame_guidance: Preserve Dibiasky's whole face and shoulders; place the short policy relabel over the open upper-right office background, well clear of her expression.
ideas.why_it_works: The movie title becomes the administration’s entire catastrophe policy, compressing denial and governance failure into four source-native words.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely neutral. The most recognizable phrase in the source doubles cleanly as a disastrous policy label. Main reservation: The slogan belongs to the later public campaign, while this frame is the earlier Oval Office briefing.
critic.strongest_quality: The most recognizable phrase in the source doubles cleanly as a disastrous policy label.
critic.main_risk: The slogan belongs to the later public campaign, while this frame is the earlier Oval Office briefing.

ideas.source_anchor: Dibiasky realizes that demanding still more evidence is not neutral when the remaining intervention window only moves in one direction.
ideas.frame_guidance: Use Dibiasky's worried reaction without any facial overlap; keep both compact lines together at lower right over open office background and let the quiet close-up carry the dread.
ideas.why_it_works: It reframes delay itself as the consequential choice, which is the scene's precise governance trap.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely neutral. It names the hidden asymmetry that makes ‘assess’ an action rather than a pause. Main reservation: Without the exact probability or canonical quote, the idea relies more heavily on the still for scene-level specificity.
critic.strongest_quality: It names the hidden asymmetry that makes ‘assess’ an action rather than a pause.
critic.main_risk: Without the exact probability or canonical quote, the idea relies more heavily on the still for scene-level specificity.

ideas.source_anchor: The military’s last-resort control measure is an orbital laser fired into Neo-Tokyo, leaving a vast destructive footprint around the target it is meant to contain.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Tetsuo's face and severed-arm wound fully visible; place the compact two-line blast-radius collision at upper left over cape and rubble, stopping before his face.
ideas.why_it_works: Calling a city-striking orbital weapon a control plan makes the intervention’s own deployment risk impossible to miss.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely neutral. It shifts the hinge from Tetsuo’s retaliation to the control intervention’s absurd collateral footprint. Main reservation: The frame proves Tetsuo’s injury more directly than the off-screen damage across Neo-Tokyo.
critic.strongest_quality: It shifts the hinge from Tetsuo’s retaliation to the control intervention’s absurd collateral footprint.
critic.main_risk: The frame proves Tetsuo’s injury more directly than the off-screen damage across Neo-Tokyo.

ideas.source_anchor: After conventional military force fails, the Colonel escalates to SOL—an orbital laser whose name literally means sun.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep Tetsuo's face and wound unobscured; set the short escalation ladder at upper left over the red cape and rubble, allowing only incidental overlap with the soft body region.
ideas.why_it_works: The name SOL turns an already deranged escalation ladder into a compact, source-native defense-in-depth joke.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely neutral. The source weapon’s name supplies the entire second beat in three words. Main reservation: The frame shows only the aftermath; viewers need enough Akira recall to know SOL is the orbital ‘sun.’
critic.strongest_quality: The source weapon’s name supplies the entire second beat in three words.
critic.main_risk: The frame shows only the aftermath; viewers need enough Akira recall to know SOL is the orbital ‘sun.’

ideas.source_anchor: The Colonel's last-resort strike leaves an extremely capable and now injured Tetsuo alive, angry, and able to retaliate.
caption_lines: A LAST RESORT WITH AN ANGRY SURVIVOR
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the full aftermath frame and preserve Tetsuo's face and wound; place the compact two-line inversion at upper left over incidental cape and rubble.
ideas.why_it_works: The reversal turns ‘last resort’ from comforting language into an irreversible escalation when the target survives it.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely neutral. It focuses on the irreversible strategic consequence instead of recycling the rejected arm-as-objective premise. Main reservation: The wording is broadly applicable and needs Tetsuo's unmistakable wounded-survivor frame to stay scene-specific.
critic.strongest_quality: It focuses on the irreversible strategic consequence instead of recycling the rejected arm-as-objective premise.
critic.main_risk: The wording is broadly applicable and needs Tetsuo's unmistakable wounded-survivor frame to stay scene-specific.

ideas.source_anchor: Homer delegates every nuclear-plant confirmation prompt to a drinking bird that repeatedly presses Y.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the exact approved one-label joke in the empty upper-left wall area; the bird, beak, keyboard, and monitor remain completely visible.
ideas.why_it_works: The bird is the whole joke and the most brutally honest diagram of rubber-stamp oversight.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely like. One iconic prop collapses performative human approval into a perfectly legible visual. Main reservation: The label has to stay left of the monitor so the bird remains the immediate focal point.
critic.strongest_quality: One iconic prop collapses performative human approval into a perfectly legible visual.
critic.main_risk: The label has to stay left of the monitor so the bird remains the immediate focal point.

ideas.source_anchor: Homer does not automate reactor judgment; he automates the gesture that lets him pretend he exercised it.
caption_lines: HOMER AUTOMATED THE PART WHERE HE PRETENDS TO CHECK.
ideas.frame_guidance: Keep the bird, beak-to-key action, and keyboard visible; place the compact sentence at upper right over the monitor casing and wall, allowing incidental overlap with the soft screen area.
ideas.why_it_works: The blunt stand-up framing distinguishes useful automation from automating away the only human judgment the process claimed to have.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely like. It isolates the exact part of human oversight Homer outsourced: pretending to inspect before approving. Main reservation: The sentence is longer than the one-label classic, so the external band must keep it effortless to scan.
critic.strongest_quality: It isolates the exact part of human oversight Homer outsourced: pretending to inspect before approving.
critic.main_risk: The sentence is longer than the one-label classic, so the external band must keep it effortless to scan.

ideas.source_anchor: A mechanical bird operates Homer's computer unattended with exactly one available action: pressing the Y key.
ideas.frame_guidance: Put the compact current-tech relabel at upper right over the monitor casing; preserve the bird, its beak-to-key geometry, and keyboard as the full visual proof.
ideas.why_it_works: Reframing Homer's toy as an early computer-use agent makes constrained tool permissions funny while showing that narrow permissions do not make delegation safe.

critic.expected_feedback: Independent prediction: likely like. The modern product category maps cleanly onto an iconic old prop without explaining the scene. Main reservation: The safety lesson is implicit in the unattended nuclear context, which the cropped workstation only partially communicates.
critic.strongest_quality: The modern product category maps cleanly onto an iconic old prop without explaining the scene.
critic.main_risk: The safety lesson is implicit in the unattended nuclear context, which the cropped workstation only partially communicates.
